candidate_findings.title: Default broad cleanup can irreversibly delete user-owned untracked work
candidate_findings.gap: `git clean -fd` cannot distinguish agent-created cruft from untracked source, documentation, or other work created by the user. The plan permits this broad operation before every run with a true default, while its explicit manual confirmation requirement is limited to ignored-file cleaning or evidence pruning.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: An ordinary run can permanently remove valuable files that Git cannot restore. Excluding Puppet Master state paths does not protect unrelated user-owned untracked files.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define a non-destructive default and an ownership boundary for automatic cleanup, or require a preview plus explicit informed consent before broad deletion. Specify a dirty-worktree gate, exact protected-path behavior, recovery/audit receipts, and acceptance fixtures proving user-owned files survive.

candidate_findings.title: The async wrapper does not guarantee cleanup on cancellation, panic, or competing errors
candidate_findings.gap: The contract only describes sequential awaits followed by returning the execution result. It does not define behavior when the wrapper future is cancelled or dropped, when execution panics, or when both execution and cleanup fail. Those paths can prevent or obscure the promised after-execution cleanup.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Cancelled runs can leave subprocesses, temporary directories, or build artifacts behind, and ambiguous error precedence can hide either the execution failure or the cleanup failure.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Specify cancellation-safe lifecycle handling, cleanup timeouts, panic boundaries where applicable, and a structured result that preserves both execution and cleanup outcomes. Add executable tests for success, runner error, cleanup error, dual error, timeout, and task cancellation.

candidate_findings.title: Mtime-based recursive pruning can delete active or recent evidence
candidate_findings.gap: The algorithm checks every file and directory by mtime and deletes old items, but directory mtime does not prove that all descendants are old. It also makes protection of currently referenced runs conditional on feasibility and provides no active-run lease, lock, or atomic snapshot contract.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A stale parent directory can contain newly updated evidence, and a background prune can race a writer. Deleting that directory can erase current acceptance evidence and corrupt lineage while a run is active.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define the prune unit using stable run or attempt identities rather than arbitrary filesystem entries, protect active units with durable leases or indexed lifecycle state, forbid deleting a directory containing retained descendants, and specify atomic concurrency, dry-run, and per-item result semantics.

candidate_findings.title: Destructive cleanup lacks a canonical-path and symlink containment contract
candidate_findings.gap: Agent-output and evidence cleanup recursively remove filesystem entries under paths formed from a supplied base, but the contract does not require canonicalizing the project root, rejecting symlinked roots or descendants, or proving each deletion target remains inside the intended project-owned directory.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A malicious or accidental symlink, path alias, or incorrect base can redirect cleanup outside the workspace and cause cross-project or home-directory data loss.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Require canonical project-root resolution, no-follow traversal, explicit symlink handling, descendant containment checks immediately before deletion, and race-resistant deletion primitives. Add adversarial tests for symlinked bases, symlink swaps, nested links, path aliases, and wrong-root input.

candidate_findings.title: The wrapper-only invariant is conventional and internally excepted
candidate_findings.gap: The plan claims the wrapper is the only entry point and guarantees consistent behavior, yet runners retain public `execute` and the app call site may bypass the wrapper. It defines neither an enforceable facade nor the authoritative predicate deciding when a working directory is known and safe.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Existing or future callers can bypass preparation and cleanup, producing provider- and call-site-dependent workspace state despite the consistency claim.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define one execution facade with a typed cleanup policy, make direct execution inaccessible outside that facade where feasible, formalize the conversation exception, and add a static or integration oracle that detects unauthorized direct `runner.execute` calls.

candidate_findings.title: Ctrl+G has no state-transition precedence between dismissing UI and aborting work
candidate_findings.gap: One key is assigned to both cancelling popovers and aborting a running response, but the contract does not define behavior when both states are active, which action consumes the event, or whether abort requires a second gesture or confirmation.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A user attempting to dismiss a transient popover can unintentionally terminate a costly response, while inconsistent focus routing can make the shortcut appear unreliable.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define a deterministic state and focus precedence table, event-consumption semantics, abort confirmation or undo behavior, and acceptance tests for popover-only, response-only, both-active, modal, composer, and IME-composition states.

candidate_findings.title: Cross-platform shortcut mapping and reserved-key conflicts remain non-normative
candidate_findings.gap: System and application shortcut conflict checks are optional, and macOS behavior is left as 'document or map.' The plan does not define physical-versus-logical key representation, modifier normalization, native text-editing precedence, reserved combinations, keyboard-layout behavior, or IME handling.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Bindings can collide with platform-standard commands, serialize inconsistently, or trigger differently across layouts and focusable controls, violating the claim that the displayed key map is the active one.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Specify canonical key serialization and event normalization, mandatory conflict classes, platform default tables, native-control and IME precedence, migration behavior, and cross-platform acceptance fixtures.

candidate_findings.title: Importing a skill silently broadens the external-directory trust boundary
candidate_findings.gap: The GUI can import or link an arbitrary existing folder, after which skill directories are automatically added to the external-directory allowlist. The contract does not require canonical-path validation, a trust review, a scoped grant, permission-before-allowlist ordering, or revocation when a skill is denied or removed.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A malicious or mistaken skill path can expand agent filesystem access beyond the project and load untrusted instructions under an apparently routine import operation.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define import trust states, canonical allowed roots, symlink policy, explicit consent showing the resulting filesystem grant, permission evaluation order, least-privilege read scope, provenance, and reliable grant revocation.

candidate_findings.title: Remove semantics do not distinguish owned skills from imported or linked folders
candidate_findings.gap: Import may create or link an existing folder, while Remove may delete 'the skill folder.' The plan does not record ownership or state whether deletion targets Puppet Master metadata, a copied skill, a link, or the user's original external directory.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Even with confirmation, the UI can authorize deletion under a misleading mental model and destroy an external skill source shared with other projects or tools.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Persist origin and ownership metadata, make Disable the safe default for imported or discovered skills, prohibit deleting non-owned sources, state symlink behavior, and make confirmation name the exact canonical path and consequences.

candidate_findings.title: Skill-name collisions are silently resolved across discovery and command namespaces
candidate_findings.gap: Discovery uses first-wins deduplication while every skill is also registered as `/skillname`. No collision warning, reserved-name list, precedence explanation, or behavior for collisions with built-in commands is specified.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A higher-priority skill can silently shadow the intended skill, and a skill command can mask or be masked by an existing command, creating an instruction-substitution risk.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define ordered precedence as a normative contract, surface all shadowed candidates and their provenance, reserve built-in command names, reject or namespace collisions, and test project/global/ancestor and command conflicts.
